newsitem.title: HONG KONG: RESEARCH ALERT- Merrill raises Swire EPS.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT- Merrill raises Swire EPS.

text.p: Merrill Lynch has raised its 1996 and 1997 earnings per share (EPS) estimates for Swire Pacific Ltd due to higher property prices and Swire's sale of the JW Marriott Hotel in Hong Kong.
In a report dated January 10, Merrill said it expected 1996 EPS of HK$4.83 compared with a previous forecast of HK$4.59, and 1997 EPS of HK$5.44 compared with HK$5.11.
"In our opinion, Swire remains one of the most undervalued conglomerates in the sector on most valuation measures," said Merrill, which has a buy rating on the stock.
It said the stock was trading at a discount to its net asset value of HK$95.40 per share.
Swire shares closed Friday morning's session at HK$72.25, up HK$0.25.
Merrill said HK$83.94 per share could be considered fair value for the stock, which offered "laggard potential".
Merrill said the stock was also trading at a price earnings ratio, based on 1997 pre-exceptional earnings, of 13 times compared with a sector average multiple of 18 times.

The report said Swire's property development business should contribute significantly higher earnings in 1997. It forecast development income of HK$2.75 billion in 1997 after development earnings of HK$638 million in 1996.
Merrill also forecast rental income to rise by 14 percent in 1997, by 17 percent in 1998 and by 14 percent in 1999.
"In 1997 and 1998 we estimate that rental income should account for 38 percent and 44 percent respectively of group net profit," it said.
But Merrill lowered its 1998 EPS estimate to HK$5.47 from HK$5.76 "due to slight delays in the completion schedules of Oxford & Lincoln Houses" in the Quarry Bay area of Hong Kong island.
